source: user-provided completed Research Handoffs in the development conversation
limitations: This registry preserves reported case facts and is not a substitute for raw probability vectors.
It must not be counted as additional sequential production OOS evidence.
AEMET physical Tmax and market resolution are intentionally excluded from the target field.

cases.lesson: Positive longer heating survived a short stall; a blanket plateau throttle would have harmed the correct late call.
Clear-sky, dry mixing, anchor, heating and cloud accumulated beyond the remaining bucket potential.
A one-hour plateau was followed by another bucket; multi-scale heating protected a justified late rise.
A 90-minute plateau was followed by a two-bucket rise; the live correction was too defensive.
The center was meteorologically close but distributed too much probability into the next integer METAR bucket.
A 90-minute plateau still ended with a one-time higher bucket touch; the positive live correction was justified.
Cloud and stronger north wind ended heating; the strongly negative late update plus conditioning was appropriate.
The daily maximum occurred at night and was not exceeded during the rainy, overcast afternoon.
A late clearing coincided with a one-time higher touch after flat short heating rates.
Five hours without temperature response outweighed positive modelled clearing and radiation signals.
A further bucket followed a 90-minute plateau; weaker wind than the prior day was an important contrast.
The modal was right after a later touch, but the 21-degree upper tail became almost as likely as the winner.
No final daily export was available; no meteorological conclusion is permitted.
Removing the clear-sky override would have restored the correct 19-degree modal.
Even a large positive anchor correction did not fully recover a shared model and TAF cold error.
Anchor, dry mixing, memory, wind and heating jointly pushed the correct bucket outside the top two.
A single higher touch followed a plateau despite only 0.1 degree of modelled remaining rise.
The first observed 23-degree touch did not justify forecasting another integer bucket.
Clear-sky helped in the morning but harmed late; the same component needs phase-dependent evaluation.
A two-hour causal plateau with zero heating did not receive enough weight against positive live components.
A first maximum touch was followed by no additional bucket despite strong anchor and dry-mixing additions.
Evidence complete did not mean observation current; the last METAR was already 30 minutes old at the late checkpoint.
A higher bucket occurred with only 0.2 degree modelled remaining rise; a blanket residual-rise cap would fail.
The warm error began before live correction; negative live evidence could not undo the raw and bias error.
The modal remained correct even though conditioning made the numerical center error larger.
Positive late components produced the next-bucket modal even though the observed maximum already matched the final target.
Flat short heating and only positive 120-minute heating did not justify the accumulated next-bucket push.
The late modal stayed correct despite a mildly warm center and no modelled remaining rise.
A negative anchor was overwhelmed by positive sky contributions despite no observed rise beyond 16 degrees.
The observed path still produced a later higher bucket; this protects against unconditional late damping.
A two-hour 19-degree plateau and zero heating conflicted with a +1.4 degree anchor.
Positive wind contribution offset negative evidence during rain, overcast and falling temperature.
The modal was correct despite a warm center; modal and center quality must remain separate.
Conditioning preserved the already observed maximum during rain and cooling instead of forecasting reheating.
